observations: Crates teach the new weapon: floating pairs, wall switches and gap crates are placed to be shot, each with a jump alternative for experts.
'Don't break this' crates (arrow box, W/TNT stack) invert the default rule; the all-box route is a restraint test.
Two-visit structure is announced (callout 4: fine to pass the unfinished outlines).
Switch placement controls backtracking: after the outlines (backtrack), high (ranged), at the end of a gem course (loop).
Explosives are keys and lids, never filler; all Nitros are sealed in the bonus.
Stacks show the collapse rule (4-stack drops two at a time) while floating columns stay put above a tool.
Density: S1 10, S2 16 (8 behind switches), S3 14 + bonus 17, S4 9, green course 12, return 9.
Time trial offers two invincibility windows placed over the side-scroll and the final belts.
Every crate pad sits between two MTATs; belt direction relative to the MTAT tells you whether to shoot or spin.

geometryObservations: **Distance is the design material of the weapon level.** Targets sit out of reach — a floating pair beside the piston lift, switches high on both walls, a ? high on the side-scroll wall, a crate over the last gap — so the bazooka replaces a risky jump (callout 2: safer than jumping; callout 7: shoot it if you fear falling), while experts keep the jump line (TT 11–13; TA5).

**Real floor breaks, unlike stage 19.** The into-screen half is a chain of slabs, stepping blocks and ring pads with ≈1–1.5 u gaps (F3 p089), the "many floor breaks" of F3 p086. The first gap pair comes before any enemy.

**The MTAT is a projectile gatekeeper at the end of a lane:** a right–left–right volley, then a green target window (F3 p086; P3 s3: dodge from the centre). It always faces down a walkway or belt toward you.

**Geometry chooses the counter.** A belt carrying you away from an MTAT gives time to shoot (callout 8); a belt carrying you toward it leaves no time, so spin (callout A). The same enemy is answered differently because of the floor.

**The BKBK becomes trivial — on purpose.** Its periodic invulnerability (lit: bazooka or super slam only) was the stage-19 timing test; the bazooka now works even when it is lit, so pairs on slabs are cleared from range. The green course then puts BKBKs where the bazooka cannot reach (P3 s16), forcing the old unlit-window answer.

**Metalnics own landings.** Callout 5 puts one on the far side of a side-scroll gap (check its spikes before jumping); three more sit under a floating crate pair and one under the finale's floating row. The bazooka only stuns them (F3 p086), so the weapon does not solve them.
**Saucers are footing.** TT bounces off one to clear the backward belt at C1 (07–08).
**Backward belts everywhere** (C1, the side-scroll belts, the finale, the green course): they lengthen exposure to missiles and make small hops the efficient gait (TA4, TA7).

**Height as a puzzle axis.** The piston lift, the hub's lower apron with a column floating above the wooden arrow, and C3's steel arrows that rebound to an upper platform (TT 23): vertical structure hides crates and keys.
**Loop topology.** The green course returns to the hub; the second pass replays the hub and the side-scroll with the outlines filled (P3 s18–s20) — the same geometry carries two crate states.

**A stepped side-scroll profile.** S3 is separate blocks at different heights with backward belts and beam fences; its test is a gap whose landing a metalnic owns, followed by a gap onto a step whose stack must be left alone (P3 s13).
**Beam fences as seasoning.** Fewer than in stage 19 (TT intro), they appear as side-scroll rods, a finale gate and green-course frames — an old mechanic reused at low density beside the new weapon.
**Bonus made of switch-built bridges.** A TNT presses the ! below its slab, a green ! is shot from range, and a high ! adds the last outline row; falling only ends the bonus.
geometryTransfer: **Projectile lane.** A `sentry` at the far end of a 3.5 m (3 u) wide, 8–10 m long walkway firing alternately left–right–left, then pausing (its exposed window); riders dodge by holding one edge, as TA2 does.

**Floor picks the counter.** Put one `sentry` at the end of a `speedpad` that pushes toward it (no time to react: ram or spin on arrival) and another behind a strip that pushes away from it (time to line up) — the callout 8 / callout A pair.
**Spinner on the landing.** A `spinner` on the far pad of a 2–2.5 m side-scroll gap, so the jump must be timed to its safe phase (callout 5); later hang a crate row 2.3 m above three `spinner`s.
**Slab chain with real gaps.** Into-screen 3.5 × 4–6 m slabs separated by 1.2–1.7 m gaps, with a single 1.7 m stepping block in the first gap and no enemy until the third slab.

**Two-level checkpoint pad.** A checkpoint pad with an upper platform 2.3–3.5 m above it, reached by a steel `trampoline` (unbreakable spring) — the C3 rebound of TT 23 — with a crate floating at the upper level.
**Loop through a hub.** End the optional course at a switch and a transfer pad back to the hub, with ordered `camnode`s for the second pass through the hub and the side-scroll.
